standard.title: Negotiate criteria and evaluate
standard.description: Negotiate design criteria including sustainability to evaluate design ideas, processes and solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use given or co-developed design criteria including sustainability to evaluate design ideas and solutions (AC9TDE4P04). They have applied provided or jointly created criteria. They have not yet negotiated criteria — the new demand is taking ownership of developing the criteria collaboratively, including sustainability as a non-optional factor.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students negotiate design criteria — including sustainability — collaboratively, and use those criteria to evaluate design ideas, processes and solutions throughout a project.

nodes.label: Negotiating design criteria collaboratively
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate to develop and agree on design criteria that will be used to evaluate a designed solution — including at least one sustainability criterion
nodes.minimum_width: Collaboratively develop at least three design criteria for a specific designed solution, including at least one sustainability criterion; explain how each criterion connects to the design's purpose
nodes.typical_width: Decide on design criteria collaboratively — discussing what the solution must achieve, what sustainability means in this context (e.g. recyclable, low waste, durable), and how to make criteria specific enough to be testable; develop criteria that distinguish between requirements and preferences
wider: Develop design criteria for a beeswax wrap product — negotiating which material properties, tool requirements and sustainability factors to include as criteria, and explaining trade-offs between competing criteria

Develop criteria for a community fundraising event — including waste reduction, attendance, funds raised and consideration of how to improve future events; explain how each criterion was negotiated among the group
Include a Safety by Design criterion in the criteria set — discussing what prevention, protection or proactive change would look like as a measurable design requirement

response_modes.reason: Students negotiating criteria for the first time tend to produce vague or unmeasurable criteria (e.g. 'it should be good'). The criteria development scaffold — what must the solution do? → how will we know it's done? → what counts as sustainable here? — produces criteria that can actually be used for evaluation.

success_criteria: Contributes at least one criterion to a collaboratively developed set
Criteria set includes at least one sustainability criterion
Each criterion is specific enough to be applied when evaluating a solution
nodes.hinge_reason: Negotiated criteria are the prerequisite for N2 — if students have not developed criteria, they have nothing to evaluate against. N2's systematic evaluation task cannot proceed without the output of N1.

nodes.label: Evaluating solutions against criteria — including processes and sustainability
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate design ideas, production processes and finished solutions against negotiated criteria — including sustainability — and identify where solutions meet or fall short
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two negotiated criteria to evaluate a design idea or solution; for each criterion, state whether it is met and provide evidence
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate designed solutions, production processes and design ideas systematically against all negotiated criteria; consider benefits and costs of production processes and environmental impact; use evaluation to determine how well criteria were met and identify what could be improved
wider: Evaluate a designed solution for an animal shelter — applying criteria related to function, materials, cost and environmental impact; documenting both what was achieved and what would be changed in a future iteration

Evaluate a school or community fundraising event against multiple criteria (waste, attendance, funds, future improvement) — gathering relevant data to support each judgement rather than relying on impression

Iterate and modify a design based on evaluation — explaining exactly what changed, which criterion drove the change, and how the modification improves the solution's performance against that criterion

response_modes.reason: Students applying criteria for the first time treat evaluation as description — listing what they did rather than judging it against a standard. Contexts with multiple, distinct criteria each requiring different evidence (a measurement, a user response, a comparison) help students build evaluation as a multi-criteria reasoning act.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The iteration-driven-by-evaluation direction is rich — students who connect a specific criterion shortfall to a specific modification are performing genuine design thinking. This is where evaluation becomes generative rather than retrospective.
success_criteria: Applies at least two criteria to evaluate a solution, with evidence for each
Identifies at least one area where the solution meets criteria and one where it falls short
